title: The Indian Statistical System: MoSPI, NSO and the NSC
breadcrumb: Official Statistics → Indian Statistical System → Institutions
engineName: Institutions and official statistics — who produces the numbers, and under what authority
provenance: Re-audited on 14 November 2026 against primary/official sources. MoSPI's Know Your Ministry document supports the ministry structure; MoSPI's NSC annual reports and the Government resolution support the Commission's origin, composition and non-statutory basis; PIB releases support the 2026 CPI, GDP and IIP base years and actual release dates. The IIP distinction is explicit: the TAC report was released on 25 May 2026, while the first monthly index release on base 2022-23 was 1 June 2026. The CPI compiler, CPI-IW compiler and WPI compiler are checked against their respective official agencies. The NSC composition is now supported by MoSPI's revised RTI manual and 2024-25 annual report, not a secondary current-affairs page. The revised RTI manual also documents the NSC's notified powers to require information, attendance and conduct statistical audits; the earlier shorthand that it simply 'cannot command' was too broad.
objectives: Name MoSPI's two wings and say what each is responsible for.
Place the NSS, the CSO and the 2019 merger into the NSO on a timeline, with the correct years.
State how the NSC was created, who sits on it, and why non-statutory is the word that matters.
Attach each major release — national accounts, IIP, CPI, CPI-IW, WPI, PLFS, the Census — to the body that produces it.
Quote the current base years of GDP, CPI and IIP and the dates they changed.
Decide which body a given task belongs to, including the tasks that fall outside MoSPI.

sheet: MoSPI: independent ministry 15 October 1999, merging the Departments of Statistics and of Programme Implementation.
Two wings: Statistics (the NSO) and Programme Implementation.
NSO's three sub-wings: Central Statistics, National Sample Survey, Data Governance — each under a Director General.
First National Sample Survey 1950; CSO 1951; CSO and NSSO merged into the NSO on 23 May 2019.
NSC: recommended by the Rangarajan review (reported 2001), resolution 1 June 2005, effective 2006, non-statutory.
NSC composition: part-time chairperson + 4 part-time members + CEO of NITI Aayog ex-officio; CSI as Secretary.
NSO compiles national accounts, IIP, CPI (R/U/C), PLFS, ASI and the NSS rounds.
CPI-IW is the Labour Bureau's; WPI is the Office of the Economic Adviser's; the Census is the RGI's.
Base years from 2026: CPI 2024 (12 Feb 2026), GDP 2022-23 (27 Feb 2026), IIP 2022-23 (first monthly release 1 June 2026).
Programme Implementation wing: IPMD monitors 11 infrastructure sectors and projects of ₹150 crore and above.
MPLADS: ₹5 crore per MP per year, run through the eSAKSHI portal since April 2023.
HCES 2022-23 released February 2024; the previous published round was 2011-12; the 2017-18 round was withheld.
PLFS moved to monthly bulletins from January 2025; NSS rounds moved to tablet-based CAPI from the 80th round.

CPI to the NSO, CPI-IW to the Labour Bureau, WPI to the Economic Adviser.

shortcuts: Any date in this topic ends in 0, 1, 9 or 5: NSS 1950, CSO 1951, MoSPI 1999, NSC resolution 2005, merger 2019.
The NSC is not a statutory regulator; however, its notified mandate includes powers to require information and conduct statistical audits. Do not reduce it to a body with no powers.
If a statement puts the Census inside MoSPI, it is false.

remember: 23 May 2019 — the CSO and NSSO became the NSO. If one date survives to the exam hall, make it this one.
The NSC is non-statutory. More marks turn on that one word than on any other fact in the module.
traps: Calling the NSC statutory or constitutional.

The NSC is resolution-based rather than statutory. It is advisory, but its notified powers include requiring documents, information and attendance, and conducting statistical audits. Do not confuse lack of statutory status with having no powers.
The Census belongs to the Registrar General under the Ministry of Home Affairs, not to MoSPI.
The first National Sample Survey (1950) preceded the Central Statistical Organisation (1951).
CPI-IW is the Labour Bureau's and the WPI is the Office of the Economic Adviser's; only CPI R/U/C is the NSO's.
The NSO is a wing of MoSPI, not a ministry in its own right.
After February 2026 the CPI base is 2024 and GDP and IIP are on 2022-23; the old 2011-12 and 2012 bases are superseded.
MoSPI's second wing is examinable: ₹150 crore project threshold, ₹5 crore MPLADS entitlement.

scenes.title: Before the lesson — four things it will assume
scenes.objective: Separate the four kinds of body this topic keeps apart: a ministry, an office, a commission and an institute.
body: This is the one topic in the paper where nothing has to be derived and everything has to be right. The questions are single facts — which body does what, which year, which merger — and they are either known or they are not.

After a gap the usual problem is not that the names are forgotten but that they have blurred together: ministry, office, commission and institute get used as if they were the same kind of thing. They are not, and almost every trap in this topic lives in that confusion. Four checks, then the lesson proper.

items.ask: What is the difference between a ministry, an office under it, and a commission?
items.recall: A ministry is the political and administrative unit of government, headed by a minister with a Secretary under him. An office is the executive machinery inside a ministry that actually produces the work. A commission is an advisory body set up to oversee or recommend, standing outside the executive line of command.
refresh: Hold the three apart by asking who takes the decision, who does the work, and who is consulted.

MoSPI is the ministry: it has a minister, a Secretary, a budget and the authority. The NSO is the office inside it that compiles the national accounts and runs the surveys. The NSC is the commission: it advises on standards, priorities and quality, and recommends — it does not run surveys itself.

The Indian Statistical Institute is a fourth kind of thing again — an institution of national importance, an academic body, not part of the ministry at all. Keeping these four apart is most of this topic.

items.ask: What does it mean for a body to be statutory, and what is the NSC?
items.recall: A statutory body is created by an Act of Parliament and draws its powers from that Act. The NSC was created by a government resolution, not an Act, so it is non-statutory — an executive body whose authority is the government's own order.
refresh: Three ways a body comes into being: a constitutional body is named in the Constitution (the Election Commission, the CAG); a statutory body is created by an Act (the SEBI, the UGC); an executive or non-statutory body is created by a government resolution or order, which the government can amend at will.

The NSC sits in the third category. A draft NSC Bill to give it statutory standing has been discussed for years and has not been enacted, so 'the NSC is a statutory body' is false as the paper stands.
This is exactly the kind of distinction a one-mark question is built on, because it can be tested in four words.

items.ask: What is a base year in an index, and why does it get revised?
items.recall: The base year is the reference period whose value is set to 100 (or whose prices and weights the series is built on). It is revised periodically so that the basket, the weights and the methods reflect the economy as it is now rather than a decade ago.
refresh: An index number compares the present with a fixed reference point. If the CPI basket still weights what households bought in 2012, it measures a cost of living nobody has any more — the share spent on telecommunications, on processed food, on fuel has all moved.
So the base is periodically shifted forward and the series is recomputed. This matters for this topic because the base years and the dates of their revision are precisely what gets asked.
Carry the distinction between the base year of an index (CPI, IIP) and the base year of the national accounts (GDP). They are revised on separate exercises, though in 2026 all three moved together.

items.ask: What is a sample survey round, and what is a census?
items.recall: A census enumerates every unit in the population. A sample survey covers a probability sample and infers the whole from it. The NSS runs in numbered rounds, each round a fresh survey on a stated subject, typically spanning a year.
refresh: The Population Census is a complete count, conducted by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner under the Census Act, 1948 — not by MoSPI. That division of labour is itself examinable.

The National Sample Survey is a sample, run by the NSS wing of the NSO, and its rounds are numbered consecutively from the first in 1950–51. A round has a subject: consumption expenditure, employment and unemployment, health, and so on, with the subjects rotating on a cycle.
So 'the NSS conducts the Census' is false, and so is 'the Census is a large sample survey'. Each sentence crosses the line this check exists to draw.

scenes.title: Who actually produces the number in the headline?
scenes.objective: See the statistical system as a chain of bodies, each with one job, rather than a list of acronyms.
body: A headline says retail inflation was 3.1% last month. Before that number existed, somebody had to decide what a representative household buys, send people to specific shops in specific towns to record prices, check the returns, compute an index against a reference year, and publish it on a fixed date whether the number is convenient or not.

Every one of those steps belongs to a named body, and the exam asks which. The price collectors are the field arm. The index is compiled by the price statistics side of the National Statistics Office. The ministry above it is MoSPI. The body that reviews whether the method is sound and the release calendar is being honoured is the National Statistical Commission, which recommends but does not compile.

That is the whole architecture: a ministry with two wings, a statistics office inside it that does the work, and a commission alongside that advises on standards. Everything else in this topic is detail hung on that frame.

There is one more thing worth noticing before the names start. This system is unusually old. India was running a national sample survey in 1950, three years after independence, when very few countries ran one at all, and the machinery built then is still recognisable in the machinery now. The questions about dates are really questions about that continuity.

aside.h: The sentence to carry into the exam
aside.body: MoSPI decides and funds, the NSO produces, the NSC advises. A question that attributes compilation to the Commission, or policy to the field staff, is testing exactly this line.

ask.q: Why is it a problem if the body that compiles a statistic is also the only body that judges its quality?
ask.nudge: Think about who is embarrassed when a number comes out badly, and who would have to admit it.

scenes.title: The ministry and its two wings
scenes.objective: Fix MoSPI's structure: when it was formed, its two wings, and what the non-statistical wing does.

blocks.body: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation became an independent ministry on 15 October 1999, formed by merging the Department of Statistics with the Department of Programme Implementation. That merger is why a statistics ministry also monitors infrastructure projects and an MP's local area scheme — the second half of its name is not decoration.

blocks.h: Wing 1 — Statistics, which is the NSO
blocks.body: The statistics wing is the National Statistics Office. It carries three sub-wings, each headed by a Director General: Central Statistics (economic statistics, national accounts, social statistics, price statistics), National Sample Survey (household surveys, enterprise surveys, field operations, coordination and quality control), and Data Governance (capacity development, international cooperation, administrative statistics, data informatics, the subordinate statistical service).

Two sub-wings. The Infrastructure and Project Monitoring Division monitors eleven key infrastructure sectors and every central sector project costing ₹150 crore or more. The MPLADS Division runs the Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme, under which each MP has ₹5 crore a year for works recommended in the constituency; it has been administered end to end through the eSAKSHI portal since April 2023. The Twenty Point Programme is also monitored from this wing.

blocks.h: Why the second wing is examinable
blocks.body: Candidates revise the statistics half and skip the rest, so the ₹150 crore threshold and the ₹5 crore MPLADS entitlement are favourite one-mark questions precisely because they sit in the half nobody reads.

blocks.h: The ministry is not the office
blocks.body: MoSPI is the ministry; the NSO is its statistics wing. 'The NSO is a ministry' and 'MoSPI conducts the NSS rounds' are both wrong, the second subtly so: the rounds are conducted by the NSS wing of the NSO, which sits inside MoSPI.

flow.caption: MoSPI, end to end — the two wings and what hangs under each

scenes.title: Three dates that carry the whole history
scenes.objective: Place the NSS, the CSO and the 2019 merger on a line, and say what survived each change.

blocks.body: Launched on P. C. Mahalanobis's design, three years after independence. The NSS directorate was placed under the Cabinet Secretariat in 1957. The round numbering runs continuously from that first survey, which is why the rounds are now in the eighties.

Set up to compile the national accounts, following the National Income Committee that had been constituted to put national income estimation on a proper footing. The CSO is the ancestor of today's Central Statistics wing.

On 23 May 2019 the CSO and the NSSO were merged into a single National Statistics Office under MoSPI. The names CSO and NSSO survive in older papers and in everyday speech, but as organisations they were folded into the NSO.

blocks.h: What the merger was for, and what was said against it
blocks.body: The stated purpose was to end duplication and give one office end-to-end responsibility from survey design to release. The criticism at the time was that it removed a layer of separation between the body that designs a survey and the body that publishes its results. A question may ask for either; both are defensible as fact about the debate, not as a verdict.

The survey came first (1950), the national accounts office second (1951). Candidates routinely reverse them because the CSO sounds more senior. And the ministry (1999) is younger than both by half a century.

scenario.teaser: A household consumption survey nobody had run for eleven years.
scenario.title: HCES 2022-23 and the eleven-year gap
body: The Household Consumption Expenditure Survey is how India learns what households actually spend on, and the weights in the consumer price index ultimately rest on it. A round was conducted in 2017-18 and its results were not released; the government held that the data quality was inadequate, while critics held that the findings were inconvenient. Either way the published series had a hole in it.

The next round was conducted in 2022-23 and its results were released in February 2024 — the first full consumption survey published since 2011-12. Eleven years is a very long time in a changing economy, and everything that depends on the consumption basket had been running on stale weights in the meantime.

That is the practical reason the release calendar and the independence of the statistical system are treated as serious questions rather than administrative detail, and it is why the National Statistical Commission's advisory role over standards and dissemination keeps appearing in the news and in the paper.
For the exam the facts to carry are plain: HCES 2022-23, results released February 2024, the previous published round 2011-12, and the 2017-18 round withheld.
scenario.close: A gap in a survey series is not an academic matter: every index that uses its weights ages with it.

scenes.title: Pause and recall
scenes.objective: Retrieve the frame before the detail piles up — retrieval is what fixes institutional facts.
scenes.intro: Answer each one out loud before you look. Covering the answer and guessing badly is worth more than reading the answer cleanly, because this topic is tested entirely on retrieval.

items.q: When did MoSPI become an independent ministry, and by merging what?
items.a: 15 October 1999, by merging the Department of Statistics and the Department of Programme Implementation.
The Statistics wing, which is the National Statistics Office, and the Programme Implementation wing.

items.q: What were the CSO and the NSSO, and what happened to them?
items.a: The CSO (1951) compiled the national accounts; the NSSO ran the sample surveys. They were merged into the National Statistics Office on 23 May 2019.

items.q: Is the National Statistical Commission statutory?
items.a: No. It was created by a government resolution of 1 June 2005 and became effective in 2006; a bill to make it statutory has been drafted but not enacted.

items.q: Which body conducts the Population Census?
items.a: The Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs — not MoSPI.

scenes.title: The National Statistical Commission
scenes.objective: State how the NSC was created, who sits on it, what it does, and the one word that limits it.

blocks.body: A commission chaired by Dr C. Rangarajan reviewed the Indian statistical system and reported in 2001. Its central recommendation was a permanent body to set standards and oversee quality. The government acted on it by a resolution dated 1 June 2005, and the National Statistical Commission came into effect in 2006.

A part-time Chairperson and four part-time Members, each with specialisation in a statistical field; one ex-officio Member (the CEO of NITI Aayog); and the Chief Statistician of India — who is also Secretary to the Government of India in MoSPI — as Secretary to the Commission. Five appointed seats plus one ex-officio, with the CSI as Secretary: that arithmetic is the question.

Evolves policies, priorities and standards for official statistics; works with central and state agencies to improve the quality of statistical products and processes; and advises on the dissemination and release calendar. It recommends; it does not compile and it does not command.

The single most examined fact about the NSC. It is an executive body created by resolution, not an Act, so it has no statutory powers over the agencies it advises. Any option calling it a constitutional or statutory body is wrong.
Who chairs the Commission changes every few years, and a paper is unlikely to ask. What it will ask is the number of members, the ex-officio seat, who acts as Secretary, and the status of the body.

scenes.title: What the NSO actually publishes, and the 2026 base revision
scenes.objective: Attach the main releases to the right body and carry the current base years.

blocks.body: National Accounts, including the GDP estimates on their fixed calendar of advance, provisional and revised estimates; the Index of Industrial Production monthly; the Consumer Price Index monthly; the Periodic Labour Force Survey; the Annual Survey of Industries; and the household and enterprise survey rounds of the NSS.

MoSPI revised the base years of all three headline series. The new CPI series, base year 2024, was released on 12 February 2026. The new GDP series, base year 2022-23, was released on 27 February 2026. For IIP, the Technical Advisory Committee report was released on 25 May 2026, and the first monthly index release on base 2022-23 followed on 1 June 2026. The series they replaced were on 2011-12 for GDP and IIP and 2012 for the CPI.

The CPI (Rural, Urban and Combined) is compiled by the NSO. The CPI for Industrial Workers is compiled by the Labour Bureau, a different body under a different ministry. The Wholesale Price Index belongs to the Office of the Economic Adviser in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. Three price indices, three owners — a standing source of questions.

The Periodic Labour Force Survey moved to monthly bulletins from January 2025. NSS rounds have moved to tablet-based computer-assisted personal interviewing under the Statistical System Strengthening Programme launched in 2024, the 80th round being the first conducted fully that way.

blocks.h: The inflation target is the RBI's, not MoSPI's
blocks.body: MoSPI compiles the CPI; the 4% target with a ±2% tolerance band is the monetary policy framework operated by the Reserve Bank. Compiling the measure and targeting it are two different institutions' jobs.

scenario.teaser: In February 2026 three headline series changed their base year in the same fortnight.
scenario.title: Why a base year revision is a national event
body: On 12 February 2026 the consumer price index moved to a 2024 base, and on 27 February the national accounts moved to a 2022-23 base. The Technical Advisory Committee report for the new IIP series was released on 25 May, and the first monthly index release followed on 1 June 2026. Three numbers that anchor monetary policy, budget forecasting and every contract indexed to inflation were recomputed within a few months.

A base revision is not a cosmetic update. It changes the basket of goods the price index tracks and the weights attached to them, and it changes the sectoral composition the national accounts are built from. Growth rates before and after a revision are not strictly comparable, which is why the ministry runs consultative workshops and publishes back-series before the switch rather than announcing it on the day.

The deeper reason the exercise matters is comparability over time against relevance to the present. Keep an old base and the series stays comparable but drifts away from the economy it is supposed to measure; move the base and the measure becomes relevant but the long series acquires a joint. Every statistical office in the world lives with that trade-off, and manages it by revising on a regular cycle rather than when the numbers become embarrassing.
For the paper, carry the three new base years and the two dates. For understanding, carry the trade-off, because that is what a question about 'why revise the base year' is actually asking.
scenario.close: A base year is a promise about what the index is measuring, and it has to be renewed before it expires.

scenes.title: Route each task to the right body
scenes.objective: Apply the architecture rather than recite it — the format most likely to appear as a matching question.
scenes.problem: For each task, name the body responsible: (a) compiling the all-India Consumer Price Index; (b) enumerating every person in the country; (c) recommending the standards an official statistic must meet; (d) monitoring a central sector project costing ₹300 crore; (e) compiling the Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers.
hints: Sort them first into three buckets: statistics production, advice on standards, and things that belong to another ministry altogether.
Two of the five are not done by the National Statistics Office at all. One is the census; the other is a price index with a different owner.
For (d), remember which wing of MoSPI the project monitoring sits in, and what its cost threshold is.

solution.say: (a) The price statistics side of Central Statistics, within the NSO, under MoSPI.
(b) The Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
(c) The National Statistical Commission, which recommends rather than compiles.
(d) The Infrastructure and Project Monitoring Division of the Programme Implementation wing: ₹300 crore is above the ₹150 crore threshold at which central sector projects are monitored.
(e) The Labour Bureau, under the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

scenes.answer: NSO; RGI; NSC; IPMD (Programme Implementation wing); Labour Bureau.
scenes.check: Two of the five sit outside MoSPI entirely. If you placed all five inside the ministry, you have merged the system with the government.

scenes.title: Six statements — verdict on each before you look
scenes.objective: Meet the exact wordings that make a true statement false.
scenes.intro: Each of these is either the standard fact or a one-word corruption of it. Decide before opening the reason.

items.claim: The National Statistical Commission is a statutory body established by an Act of Parliament.
items.why: It was created by a government resolution dated 1 June 2005 and is non-statutory. A bill to give it statutory standing has been drafted but not enacted.

items.claim: The NSO was formed in 2019 by merging the CSO and the NSSO.
items.why: 23 May 2019, under MoSPI. The older names survive in speech and in past papers, but the organisations were merged.

items.claim: MoSPI conducts the Population Census every ten years.
items.why: The Census is conducted by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India under the Ministry of Home Affairs. MoSPI runs sample surveys, not the complete enumeration.

items.claim: The Chief Statistician of India serves as Secretary to the National Statistical Commission.
items.why: The CSI, who is also Secretary to the Government of India in MoSPI, acts as Secretary of the Commission.

items.claim: The Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers is compiled by the National Statistics Office.
items.why: CPI-IW is compiled by the Labour Bureau under the Ministry of Labour and Employment. The NSO compiles CPI Rural, Urban and Combined.

items.claim: The Programme Implementation wing of MoSPI monitors central sector projects costing ₹150 crore and above.
items.why: That is the Infrastructure and Project Monitoring Division's remit, alongside eleven key infrastructure sectors.

scenes.title: Transfer — a case the lesson has not shown you
scenes.objective: Reason from the architecture to a situation you have not been given the answer to.
scenes.problem: A state government publishes an employment figure that contradicts the national survey. A newspaper asks who can settle the discrepancy, and whether the Centre can compel the state to change its method. Answer both parts using what you know about how the system is constituted.
hints: The question is about authority, not about statistics. Start by asking which bodies have any authority at all.
One body's whole job is standards and quality across central and state agencies. Ask what instrument it holds.
Recall what 'non-statutory' means in practice when the other party is a state government.

solution.say: The body whose remit covers this is the NSC: evolving standards and working with central and state agencies on the quality of statistical products is exactly its stated function.

But the NSC is resolution-based, not a statutory regulator. It can require documents, information and attendance and conduct statistical audits. It can recommend that a State adopt standards, but the resolution does not give it a general power to issue binding directions compelling adoption.
solution.math: Resolution-based → advisory, but with notified information and statistical-audit powers

solution.say: Nor can MoSPI simply order it. Statistics appears in the Union, State and Concurrent lists in different respects, and a state's own statistical system is its own. The practical instruments are the Indian Statistical Service cadre, common concepts and definitions, central funding of state capability and publication of the divergence — persuasion and transparency rather than command.
solution.math: Centre → standards, funding, publication; not direction

scenes.answer: The NSC is the right forum, but it can only recommend; neither it nor MoSPI can compel a state to change its method, so the lever is standard-setting, capability support and publishing the difference.
scenes.check: If your answer was 'the NSC can order the state to comply', the word non-statutory has not landed yet. That is the single idea this transfer is testing.

scenes.title: What you should now be able to do unaided
scenes.objective: Compress the topic to what will survive until the exam.
body: Name the ministry, its year and its two wings: MoSPI, 1999, Statistics (the NSO) and Programme Implementation.
Place the three dates on a line: the first National Sample Survey in 1950, the Central Statistical Organisation in 1951, the merger of the CSO and NSSO into the NSO on 23 May 2019.

State the NSC's origin, composition and limit: recommended by the Rangarajan commission's 2001 review, created by resolution on 1 June 2005, effective 2006; a part-time chairperson, four part-time members, the CEO of NITI Aayog ex-officio, the Chief Statistician of India as Secretary; non-statutory throughout.

Attach each release to its owner: national accounts, IIP, CPI (Rural, Urban, Combined), PLFS and ASI to the NSO; CPI-IW to the Labour Bureau; WPI to the Office of the Economic Adviser; the Census to the Registrar General.

Carry the current base years: CPI on 2024 from 12 February 2026; GDP on 2022-23 from 27 February 2026; IIP on 2022-23, with the TAC report on 25 May and the first monthly index release on 1 June 2026 — replacing 2012 and 2011-12 respectively.
Know the two numbers from the second wing: ₹150 crore as the central sector project monitoring threshold, ₹5 crore a year as the MPLADS entitlement per Member of Parliament.
